hook.line: When a story has a hero and a villain, Spanish uses two small phrases to tell you who is who. The news this week has plenty of both.
hook.es: Gracias a Mariana, todos conocen la historia.
hook.en: Thanks to Mariana, everyone knows the story.

examples.es: Gracias a ti llegamos a tiempo.
examples.en: Thanks to you we made it on time.

examples.es: Gracias a que llovió, se salvó la cosecha.
examples.en: Thanks to the fact that it rained, the harvest was saved.

examples.es: Perdimos el vuelo por culpa del trancón.
examples.en: We missed the flight because of the traffic jam.

examples.es: Por culpa de Altamira, el barrio está en peligro.
examples.en: Because of Altamira, the neighbourhood is in danger.

examples.es: Gracias al artículo, todos conocen la verdad.
examples.en: Thanks to the article, everyone knows the truth.

examples.es: Todo salió mal por culpa mía.
examples.en: Everything went wrong because of me.

rule:
Both phrases say "because of", but they carry opposite feelings. *Gracias a* is for a good result: someone or something to thank. *Por culpa de* is for a bad result: someone or something to blame.

Both are followed by a noun: *gracias a ti*, *por culpa del trancón*. Remember the contractions: *a + el = al* and *de + el = del*.

For a whole clause, use *gracias a que* with a normal verb: *Gracias a que llovió*. After *por culpa*, a person can come as *mía*, *tuya*, *suya*: *por culpa mía*.

The neutral version, with no praise and no blame, is *debido a* or *a causa de*.
smallPrint: Teachers call these causal prepositional phrases. *Gracias a* adds a positive tone and *por culpa de* a negative one.

readAndPick.es: Gracias a ti llegamos a tiempo.
options: We were late because of you.
Thanks to you we made it on time.
We made it on time, but not thanks to you.

readAndPick.es: Perdimos el vuelo por culpa del trancón.
options: We missed the flight because of the traffic jam.
Thanks to the traffic jam we caught the flight.

readAndPick.es: Gracias a Mariana, todos conocen la historia.
options: Everyone knows the story because Mariana is to blame.
Thanks to Mariana, everyone knows the story.

readAndPick.es: Por culpa de Altamira, el barrio está en peligro.
options: Thanks to Altamira, the neighbourhood is safe.
Because of Altamira, the neighbourhood is in danger.

readAndPick.es: Gracias a que llovió, se salvó la cosecha.
options: Thanks to the fact that it rained, the harvest was saved.
The harvest was lost because of the rain.

readAndPick.es: Todo salió mal por culpa mía.
options: Everything went wrong because of me.
Everything went well thanks to me.
Everything went wrong because of you.

readAndPick.es: Por culpa del incendio, cerraron la calle.
options: Because of the fire, they closed the street.
Thanks to the fire, they opened the street.

readAndPick.es: Gracias al artículo, todos conocen la verdad.
options: Because of the official, the article is suspended.
Thanks to the article, everyone knows the truth.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *Gracias a* or *Por culpa de*: ___ ti llegamos a tiempo. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Gracias a ti llegamos a tiempo.
yourTurn.why: Arriving on time is good news, so we thank: *gracias a*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *gracias* or *culpa*: Perdimos el vuelo por ___ del trancón. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Perdimos el vuelo por culpa del trancón.
yourTurn.why: Missing the flight is bad, so the traffic gets the blame: *por culpa de*.

yourTurn.prompt: Because of Altamira, the neighbourhood is in danger.
yourTurn.answer: Por culpa de Altamira, el barrio está en peligro.
accept: El barrio está en peligro por culpa de Altamira.
yourTurn.why: A bad result, so *por culpa de*.

yourTurn.prompt: Thanks to the article, everyone knows the truth.
yourTurn.answer: Gracias al artículo, todos conocen la verdad.
accept: Todos conocen la verdad gracias al artículo.

yourTurn.prompt: Thanks to the fact that it rained, the harvest was saved. Use *que*.
yourTurn.answer: Gracias a que llovió, se salvó la cosecha.
accept: Gracias a que llovió, la cosecha se salvó.
yourTurn.why: A whole clause after *gracias a* needs *que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Everything went wrong because of me.
yourTurn.answer: Todo salió mal por culpa mía.
accept: Todo salió mal por mi culpa.
yourTurn.why: With a person, *por culpa mía* is the natural form.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it blame: *Gracias al trancón llegamos tarde.*
yourTurn.answer: Por culpa del trancón llegamos tarde.
yourTurn.why: Arriving late is bad news, so *por culpa de*. *De + el* joins into *del*.

pitfalls.wrong: Gracias a el artículo, todos lo saben.
pitfalls.right: Gracias al artículo, todos lo saben.

pitfalls.wrong: Por culpa a Altamira, perdimos el café.
pitfalls.right: Por culpa de Altamira, perdimos el café.
pitfalls.why: The blame phrase ends in *de*, not *a*.

pitfalls.wrong: Gracias al incendio, perdimos la casa.
pitfalls.right: Por culpa del incendio, perdimos la casa.
pitfalls.why: Losing a house is not something to thank anyone for. Blame needs *por culpa de*.

personal: Think of someone who helped you this week and something that annoyed you. Thank the first with *gracias a* and blame the second with *por culpa de*.
